text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: p99 latency SLO breach on streaming endpoints (region: us-west-2). Alert rule: streaming_p99 > 1200ms for 5m. Affected pool: shared-gpu-pool-3. Rough estimate: ~14% of streaming requests experiencing stalls.

morgan (oncall): seeing it. p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 2.1s, lots of chunk retransmits. Which tenants on pool-3?

sam (sre): tenant list from scheduler: tenant-a, tenant-b, tenant-c, tenant-heavy (unknown). I/O metrics show NVMe bandwidth saturation on hosts gpu-uw3-[12,13,14].

anya (runtime): streaming telemetry shows many stalls at token boundary ~chunk-size=256. KV cache hit rates drop for some sessions. Could be eviction pressure.

lee (ml-infra): pulling iostat/fio now. quick snippet:
```
# iostat -x 1 3
Device:         r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz  await svctm  %util
nvme0n1       102.00  120.00  81920  120000   1400.00   12.30  9.42   0.85  98.5
```
This is NVMe saturating, %util ~98.5 on those hosts.

morgan (oncall): any noisy-tenant signatures? which tenant is driving nvme?

sam (sre): metric top: tenant-heavy is responsible for ~60% of write throughput and large sequential writes (checkpointing / model-save bursts). Also see cgroup blkio.throttle.io_service_bytes causing throttles.

anya (runtime): logs show repeated KV cache evictions and worker stalls:
```
2024-05-04T13:00:12Z worker[312]: kvcache: eviction triggered, evicting 24 entries, current_size=98%
2024-05-04T13:00:18Z stream[87]: send stalled waiting on IO write (err=EIO_TIMEOUT)
```

lee (ml-infra): digging cgroup settings on gpu-uw3-12:
```
# cat /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/tenant-heavy/blkio.throttle.bps_device
8:0 104857600
```
tenant-heavy is capped but also hammering small writes causing high IOPS + queue depth.

frank (customer-success): FYI a handful of customers reported degraded streaming quality; one support ticket flagged live call stuttering. Customer visible impact: intermittent output delays ~2-3s.

morgan (oncall): immediate live mitigations: 1) reduce tenant-heavy concurrency 2) move tenant-heavy off shared-gpu-pool-3 to dedicated hot-swap pool 3) apply temporary application-level rate limit / backpressure for streaming on that tenant 4) mark pool as degraded to avoid new sessions. Which we can do fastest?

sam (sre): easiest quick win: throttle tenant-heavy at scheduler layer (concurrency cap) and mark pool degraded. I can push concurrency cap in 2-3 min. Moving tenant requires scheduler placement and warmup.

anya (runtime): I can flip prefix cache to aggressive TTL and disable big-checkpoint flushes temporarily for tenant-heavy (reduce write bursts). Need approval. Patch: set KV_CACHE_TTL=10s for tenant-heavy.

lee (ml-infra): to move tenant-heavy we need: cordon node(s), drain pods, taint schedule or set nodeSelector to dedicated-pool. That takes ~10-15m and higher risk.

morgan (oncall): ok do the low-risk steps now. Sam do concurrency cap + mark pool degraded. Anya do cache TTL and disable checkpoint flushes. Lee start placement plan and keep moving if we still see >1.5s p99 after 10m. Frank please prepare customer comms note.

sam (sre): running command to update scheduler policy:
```
# schedulerctl set-concurrency tenant-heavy 2 --pool shared-gpu-pool-3
OK: concurrency updated
```
Applying pool degraded flag:
```
# infractl pool set-status shared-gpu-pool-3 degraded --reason "IO saturation"
OK
```

anya (runtime): patch applied to runtime config for tenant-heavy: KV_CACHE_TTL=10s, CHECKPOINT_FLUSH=false. Watching effects.

(5m pass)

morgan (oncall): p95 now ~380ms, p99 ~1.1s. Good improvement but still above target <1s p99.

sam (sre): NVMe util down to ~75% on hosts, but I/O spikes remain on one host gpu-uw3-13. Lee: resume placement?

lee (ml-infra): starting live migration: will cordon gpu-uw3-13 and evict tenant-heavy pods -> target dedicated-warm-pool nodes. Kickoff: `kubectl drain gpu-uw3-13 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

deployment-bot: scheduled eviction tasks for pods: tenant-heavy-worker-{0..3} on gpu-uw3-13. ETA 4m.

morgan (oncall): During migration, enable fallback model variant for streaming requests from tenant-heavy (lower resource QPS). Anya: can we route to lightweight variant?

anya (runtime): yes toggling model-variant-routing for tenant-heavy to model-small-quantized now.

(10m pass)

lee (ml-infra): migration complete for gpu-uw3-13. Node drained and cordoned. NVMe %util across pool nodes now <60%.

morgan (oncall): p99 trending 700-850ms. Still a few residual stalls. Any lingering IO bursts?

sam (sre): tail logs show some streaming retransmits for sessions started before mitigation. Most new sessions look fine. We'll let existing sessions finish or force reconnect for heavy sessions.

frank (customer-success): preparing customer note: short incident summary, mitigations, ETA to full recovery. Asking for list of affected customer IDs to include.

morgan (oncall): frank, use internal incidents page -> run `query: streaming_slow_by_tenant tenant-heavy` to fetch impacted customer IDs.

(30m pass)

morgan (oncall): p99 stable ~420ms, p95 ~360ms. Marking incident as mitigated but not resolved. We will do follow-ups: post-mortem, permanent placement for tenant-heavy, consider adjusting blkio cgroup policy to avoid write bursts, add early-warning metric on nvme util > 85% for 3m.

sam (sre): follow ups: add autoscale buffer for NVMe and adjust eviction heuristics to avoid synchronous checkpoint writes. Also add streaming stall synthetic checks.

lee (ml-infra): action: schedule tenant-heavy to dedicated reserved pool with quota and throttle policy. Also evaluate moving checkpoint writes to object-store asynchronous path.

anya (runtime): action: add per-tenant cache pressure telemetry and auto-TTL when eviction >75%.

frank (customer-success): cc customers with status update and offer credits to impacted customers (CS to own).

morgan (oncall): handing off to night oncall: @lee you are next in rotation. Keep watch for recurrence; if p99 > 1.2s for 10m escalate back to oncall SRE. Link to runbook: https://intra.redwood/ops/runbooks/streaming-tail-latency.

lee (ml-infra): acked. I'll keep alerts on and follow up in a postmortem doc.

incident-bot: Incident marked MITIGATED by morgan at 1718540400.

morgan (oncall): thanks all :thumbsup: great quick coordination.
